prompt:
Task: extract structured data from 326 SVB payment notification emails in a Gmail mailbox (user_email "me" = robert@harmonygames.co) and write to a CSV file.

The message IDs are in /app/svbids.json (JSON array) and pre-split into 12-ID chunks, one JSON array per line, in /app/chunks.txt (28 lines). For each line, call mcp__hg__gmail_get_messages_batch with message_ids = that array, format="full", user_email="me". Results will be too large and get saved to a file path given in the error message; that's fine. A helper /app/parse.py exists: `python3 /app/parse.py <savedfile> 3000` prints From|Subject|Date and the decoded plain-text body of each message. You can import its functions (load, body, htmlbody) in your own Python script. If plain text body is empty, try htmlbody and strip tags.

Each body looks like: "SVB Payment Notification: Payment Processed  Hello X,The following payment has been successfully processed.From: Harmony Games GAMES INC.: Analysis Checking ***0100To: Leapblock LTD ***1359Amount: 3,700.00 USDTransaction Date: Feb 02 2026Transaction ID: ... Delivery Date: Feb 03 2026Payment Reference: ...". Subjects may vary (e.g. Payment Processed, Returned, Cancelled, Failed, etc.) — record the subject exactly and also any status words in the body.

Write /app/notices.csv with columns: msg_id, email_date, subject, status_phrase (e.g. "successfully processed" or whatever the body says), from_account, to_name, to_account_last4, amount (number, no commas), currency, transaction_date (YYYY-MM-DD), delivery_date, transaction_id, payment_reference, extra (any other notable text in the body, e.g. returned/reversal reasons, FX info, memo). Use python csv module. Make sure ALL 326 messages are present (verify count, re-fetch any missed; you can call with fewer IDs if a batch errors). Run the 28 batch calls in parallel groups to be fast.

When done, report: row count, distinct subjects with counts, distinct status phrases, distinct currencies, distinct from_accounts, and a table of to_name + to_account_last4 with count and USD sum (and non-USD sums by currency), plus min/max transaction_date. Also list any rows that look unusual (non-"Processed" subjects, odd text in extra, duplicate transaction IDs).
